A. Tests that encode the OLD phone-approval contract (would break under the new policy)
1. src/lib/bunny-missions/missions.test.ts:412-424 "MA0R: phone approval serializes exactly the desktop authority..." Plan = read step A (415) + write model step B dependsOn 0 (415). Device approves via missionCommand actor "device:paired-phone", start:false (417). Asserts envelope deep-equals requestedScope after stripping id/missionId/grantedAt/grantedBy/expiresAt/revokedAt (419-420); events approval.mission_envelope and approval.remote_device (421-422). (a) BREAKS if write-model approval is refused at approve time (417 throws). (b) BREAKS at 420 if the device envelope gets writeIncludesShell=false or any marker field (419 strips only six keys). (c) survives unless model steps are treated as EXECUTE (see note in B).
2. src/lib/bunny-missions/capabilities.test.ts:264-314 "Host HTTP: snapshot stays backward compatible, mission commands are validated, remote devices are limited". modelPlan (286) = read model "Custom" + write model "Research". Device approve with start:false expects status 200 (291-292): BREAKS under (a). Line 295 deepEqual(phoneEnvelope.providers, phoneMission.requestedScope.providers): BREAKS under (b) if the device envelope providers differ (e.g. writeIncludesShell or a marker inside providers). 297 (maxSessions equal desktop) and 298 (step scopes equal) survive if 999 is clamped/ignored. 299 (grantedBy ^device:) and 301-302 (events) survive. 304 (device mission.stop) survives. 266 hard-codes port 43131.
3. src/lib/bunny-missions/approval-batches.test.ts:560-585 "T9 remote: a paired phone may grant only the offered batch, revoke its own..." Device allow_batch (567) on computer.type, which is EXECUTE (computer.server.ts:418; test manifest approval-batches.test.ts:48). Asserts createdBy device (569), target (570), usedCount 3 (572), device revoke_batch (573-575). BREAKS under (c). Lines 579-583 (unknown request refused for workstation) survive.
4. src/lib/bunny-host/remote-device.test.ts:535-542 "T9 launch rule". deviceMayLaunch({provider:"claude",model:"any"}) === false (540-541) must stay false for the no-scope call. Survives (a) only if any claude-read allowance requires an explicit scope argument.

Device path: missionCommand(env.missions,"mission.approve",{id,start:false},{local:false,actor:"device:x"}) (417) or env.missions.approve(id,"device:x"). Respond: env.missions.respond(requestId, decision, actor) (307, 584); requests via store.requests(id) (572).

- remote-device.test.ts fixture 52-97: real startHost with fake claude and ollama adapters (58-64; launch finishes after 5 ms, 32-51); helpers api/raw/state/pair/stream 68-90; fixture({agentic:true}) adds Filesystem/Terminal/Git (65). op() 107-114 is capability-only, so a model helper must be added for a model-step device test.
- remote-remediation.test.ts fixture 30-83: adapters: [] (39), so no provider can launch; device pairing 59; restart() 80; readStep 187; plainMission 188-192; missionRow 193-196.
- capabilities.test.ts 264-314: real startHost (266), fixed port 43131, no fake adapters. Only start:false approvals are safe there.

E. Important caveat for the new policy: model steps set execution=true, and scopeFor then adds EXECUTE to riskClasses (authorization.server.ts, "if (execution) risks.add('EXECUTE')" near the end of scopeFor). A refusal keyed on riskClasses containing EXECUTE would also refuse ollama-only and read-only model Missions, which breaks capabilities.test.ts:291 and missions.test.ts:417. The check must key on the step executor, the provider and the access, not on riskClasses.

result.summary: Read-only audit of model-step dispatch and provider change paths for Mission child tasks (paths are relative to C:/Users/allam/Documents/new/bun-router). Root cause: the device boundary (deviceMayLaunch / deviceRequestRefusal / deviceApproved) is applied only to direct Task approval and to waiting Mission children answered individually. A device-approved Mission plan never triggers a per-child gate. Its model children are launched through approveDelegated, which checks only taskViolation (provider-agnostic except providers.allow). Every later reroute, escalation, relaunch and restart replay of those children then runs with no device check. Routing for non-local steps requires filesystem capability (requiresFilesystem at manager.server.ts:1259-1262), which ollama lacks (adapters.server.ts:162 sets capabilities ["text"]). So a device-approved plan with a non-local model step can only resolve to claude or codex children, launched with no device check. The CONFIRMED paths are P1, P3, P4 and P6. P2 is a confirmed gap in the launch-time reroute check. P5 and P7 are suspected gaps. P8 to P10 are guarded or not reachable from a device.

So a device can approve a plan with model steps, and approval starts it at once (line 796). For each non-local model step, requiresFilesystem is true, so ollama is ineligible, and auto routing selects claude or codex. taskViolation passes unless providers.allow, budget, cwd or localOnly fail. Then approveDelegated runs with check=taskViolation only. No device check and no deviceApproved marker is set. The provider.execute ask (line 1367-1381) is raised only on violation, so a permitted envelope never asks. For a remote envelope, submit children with constraints that exclude claude and codex by construction: providerAllowlist: ["ollama"] (or the intersection of the existing allowlist and ollama), localOnly: true, requiresFilesystem: false (the ollama capability set is text only, adapters.server.ts:162, so requiresFilesystem must be false or ollama is ineligible), and modelAllowlist limited to verified local, non-remote models. Without it, the cleanest policy is that deviceMissionRefusal (manager.server.ts:1963-1977) refuses any plan whose providers.sessions contains a write-scoped or filesystem-requiring model step, and whose requestedScope includes terminal.exec or EXECUTE.

result.designNotes: Enforcement points for the new policy, from the paths above. result.summary: Read-only audit of capability execution under a device-approved envelope. The device gate (device-authority.server.ts:102-109, manager.server.ts:1953-1994) only blocks WORKSTATION_ONLY_RISKS (EXTERNAL_SIDE_EFFECT, DESTRUCTIVE) and manifests flagged sensitive or hardApproval. Every implemented EXECUTE and WRITE action therefore passes it, including terminal.exec, computer.focus/invoke/type/open_app, git.commit/merge/worktree and filesystem.write. Four confirmed bypasses follow from the code: (1) a device allow_once on any terminal.exec ask sets an action-only approvedOnce, and decide() returns allow before any envelope check (authorization.server.ts:167, ahead of 172-185), so the one-time path skips envelope.terminal, cwd, revocation, expiry and the "ask every time" rule; for a skill run it covers every terminal.exec step; (2) terminal scope binds the command name and resolved executable but never args (authorization.server.ts:114-122; types.ts:107), and there is no interpreter denylist (process.server.ts:31-42), so approved node/npm/npx/git/powershell/cmd run arbitrary argv; (3) riskFor escalation inspects only args[0] (local.server.ts:145-149), so git -C dir push and npm --prefix . install stay EXECUTE and auto-allow; (4) git commit/merge/worktree run repo hooks and merge drivers with the full user config (local.server.ts:205, git-merge.server.ts:15,44), and filesystem.write has no .git guard (authorization.server.ts:109-113), so a device-approved mission can write .git/hooks and then commit. Batches are Calculator-only (batches.server.ts:93), connectors are unimplemented (connectors.server.ts:103; bus.server.ts:162), and retries and Host restarts clear one-time approvals (manager.server.ts:2911, 3468, 3737-3761). No tests were run and no files were edited.

- git: status, diff, log, tracked_files, branch, commit_info = READ. commit, worktree_add, worktree_remove, merge = WRITE (188-191). No flags, all implemented, all device-approvable. Non-bounded hook and config exposure per pathway 6.
- notifications.send = READ (no flags).
- computer (computer.server.ts:414-421): list_windows READ; read_controls READ sensitive:true (415); focus_window EXECUTE; invoke_control EXECUTE; type EXECUTE (416-418); capture READ sensitive:true (419); open_app EXECUTE, allowlist notepad, calc, mspaint, explorer, terminal (wt.exe) (420, 13); read_calculator READ. All implemented. Only read_controls and capture are sensitive, so the other computer EXECUTE actions are device-approvable.
- browser (browser.server.ts:51-61): navigate, search, read, extract, metadata, wait, screenshot, tabs = READ; click, type, download = WRITE. No sensitive or hardApproval flags. Device-approvable.
- github (connectors.server.ts:17-20): pr_list, issue_list, repo_view = READ, implemented, fixed gh args (device-approvable). pr_create and comment = EXTERNAL hardApproval, implemented:false.
- connectors (connectors.server.ts:69-103): email, calendar, messaging, sms, whatsapp, phone. All implemented:false, so bus.server.ts:162 denies them. Nine EXTERNAL or DESTRUCTIVE items carry hard:true (e.g. email.send, calendar.create, calendar.cancel). Whether each read item has hard set was not checked individually.
- Observation: no implemented non-computer action carries hardApproval, and ALWAYS_ASK (authorization.server.ts:13) contains only EXTERNAL and DESTRUCTIVE. EXECUTE and WRITE are never always-ask inside an envelope, so the hardApproval mechanism is currently inert for every implemented action.

ONE-TIME ALLOWANCE BINDING (as built). Action name only. The PermissionRequest stores action, risk, reason and batchOffer, not params (manager.server.ts:3044-3056; the agentic fingerprint is set only for Agents, 3057-3069). Expiry is none (it is cleared on retry, 2911 and 3468, and on restart, 3737-3761). Use count is none (one invocation per allow_once, but every skill step with that action matches). The oneTime branch ignores scopeViolation, the envelope and expiry (authorization.server.ts:167). The Agent-only check at manager.server.ts:2262-2275 is the only param-level binding, and it applies only to agentic missions.

SUGGESTED POLICY SEAMS (for the implementer). (a) Classify a manifest flag such as codeExecution for interpreters, task runners (npm test, npm run), hook-triggering git ops (commit, merge, worktree_add) and UI automation; deny it in deviceApprovalRefusal, deviceMissionRefusal, deviceRequestRefusal and deviceAgenticRefusal. (b) Make the oneTime branch re-run scopeViolation, bind to operationDigest(action, params) (batches.server.ts:49), and add expiry and use count; remove it from the device path. (c) Bind terminal argv in the mission envelope, or deny interpreters by identity; scan all args in riskFor. (d) Harden all non-bounded git runs the same way as the bounded path (local.server.ts:203) and exclude .git from filesystem writes. (e) Make the device approval summary (manager.server.ts:701) show argv and targets, not only risk classes.

NOT TRACED: the phone's mission.get projection of step params and verification args; the scheduler behavior for revoked or expired envelopes with an existing approvedOnce; whether any UI-automation sequence reaches a shell; the http.server.ts device routing beyond DEVICE_RIGHTS.</designNotes>

result.summary: Principal derivation inside the Host is sound: the actor is chosen server-side from the bearer (workstation token or hashed device credential), and no client field can set actor, by, origin or local. The gateway's local-versus-remote decision is a header denylist, so a deployment whose tunnel rewrites Host to loopback without forwarding headers would hand a device the workstation token (SUSPECTED). The principal does not carry through to provider launch: a device-granted Mission envelope is admitted by envelope-only checks, and writeIncludesShell is hardcoded true, so device-approved shell work launches at approve, retry, reroute and after restart. Device self sign-out also leaves device-granted authority live. The T9R-F01 types (EnvelopeAuthority, DesktopGrant, desktopRequired, writeIncludesShell false for device grants) are declared but have no producer or consumer in src/.

pathways.name: gateway-local-decision-by-header-denylist
pathways.location: src/lib/orch/host-bridge.server.ts:9 (PROXY_HEADERS), 27-38 (local branch), 39-43 (remote branch and cookie token), 87 (hostCall token selection); node_modules/srvx/dist/adapters/node.mjs:129 (x-forwarded-host ignored unless trustProxy)
pathways.detail: authorizeBridge returns local:true when url.hostname is 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] and the TCP peer is loopback, and when none of cf-connecting-ip, cf-ray, x-forwarded-for, x-real-ip or forwarded is present and x-forwarded-proto is not https (lines 28, 34-38). Local returns before the BUNNY_REMOTE_ORIGIN check (39-41). url.hostname comes from the Host header, and srvx ignores x-forwarded-host unless trustProxy is configured, so Host is the only input. If the configured tunnel or proxy on this machine rewrites Host to loopback and adds none of the denylisted headers, a device-cookie request returns local:true. hostCall then sends the workstation token (line 87), which grants full workstation authority from the internet. Cloudflare-style tunnels add cf-ray and cf-connecting-ip, so this depends on deployment. The check is a denylist, not an allowlist, and the tunnel config is not in this repo.
pathways.recheck: Inspect the actual tunnel or proxy configuration (Host rewrite, injected headers). Simulate a request with Host: localhost:8080 from a loopback peer with no proxy headers and confirm whether hostCall would send the workstation token.

result.designNotes:
Actor and by strings in the Host. 'workstation' is set for every request that presents the workstation token (http.server.ts:413-414, actorOf at device-authority.server.ts:121-122). 'device:<uuid>' is set only for bearer-authenticated devices. Call sites that pass the actor: http.server.ts:570 (TaskManager.approve(id, actor)); commands.server.ts:51 (replan), :52 (approve), :62 (retry), :76 (respond), all access.actor; agent-runtime.server.ts:168 (missions.approve from agent.start, actor), :874 and :892 (agents.start(actor)), :893 (reauthorizeAgent(actor)); bunny-missions/manager.server.ts:3285 (tasks.approve(step.taskId, by) inside respond); approveDelegated at manager.server.ts:1387 takes no actor and is envelope-driven. Literal 'workstation' origins: manager.server.ts:971 (default), :1936, project-service.server.ts:66 and :101, commands.server.ts:38. Literal 'trigger:<id>', 'mission:<id>' and 'agent:<actor>' are origin labels only and never approvals.

Suggested fix order (not implemented, read-only audit). (1) Make envelopeFrom set authority {kind:'remote', sessionCeiling:['tool_free' or 'read_tools'], codeExecution:'desktop_only'} and writeIncludesShell:false when by starts with 'device:'. Then enforce it in providerScopeViolation, taskViolation and the reroute/retry admission, so grantedBy is checked and not just stored. (2) Gate mission.start, and recover()'s ready-to-start branch (manager.server.ts:3854), on the envelope's authority. (3) Run endDeviceGrants on self sign-out too (http.server.ts:731). (4) In authorizeBridge, make local an allowlist (configured trusted proxy, or no proxy at all) or require the BUNNY_REMOTE_ORIGIN match on the local path too. (5) Persist the operation ledger and the device-task marker, or key them to the boot epoch.

Unverified in this audit: the adapter-level claims (claudeLaunchArgs Bash/PowerShell, codex sandbox flags), agenticScopeViolation's provider.execute rule, and the actual tunnel configuration. These are outside this focus and should be checked by the other lanes. No file was edited, no tests were run, and no servers were started.
